ABT RSQ8-LE 1000 Is a Monstrous Audi RS Q8 With 1,000 Horsepower
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | abt_sportsline
ABT Sportsline has been on a roll recently, as it unveiled several cool projects, including that Audi RS 5 Avant that we covered last week.
More recently, the famous tuner has pulled the wraps off another interesting build. It is called the ABT RSQ8-LE 1000, and as mentioned in the title, it is a monstrous Audi RS Q8 with a four-digit output. We kid you not, this machine is roughly as punchy as the original Bugatti Veyron, which is the world’s first hypercar, and it remains a family-friendly machine and a very good daily.
The tuner says that the Audi RS Q8 in question has the ABT Power R performance upgrade, complete with a new turbo, an intercooler, a water/ethanol injection system, and other upgrades. The result? A massive 1,000 horsepower. The output is actually in metric horsepower, and it translates to b986 rake horsepower and 736 kilowatts. The top speed has been increased to a more exotic figure of 199 mph (320 kph).
How does it compare to the standard model? With no outside intervention, the RS Q8 has 640 ps (631 hp/571 kW), and that’s 360 ps (355 hp/265 kW) less than the ABT RSQ8-LE 1000. The twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 engine produces 850 Nm (627 lb-ft) of torque. It’s unknown how fast the tuned crossover coupe is, but the standard one hits 60 mph (97 kph) in 3.4 seconds. Flat-out, it does 155 mph (250 kph), and this number increases to 190 mph (305 kph) when ticking the RS Dynamic Package Plus box on the options list.
Photo: Instagram | abt_sportsline The vehicle also features the ABT Body Control System, which is an adaptive roll stabilization system, for a more engaged driving experience. A stainless steel exhaust system with four tailpipes, each one measuring 105 mm (4.1 in) in diameter, is also on deck, enhancing the car’s soundtrack. The model rides on ABT’s High Performance IR23 FlowForming wheels, 23 inches in diameter, which were wrapped in 295/35 tires. The alloys were painted gold, and the body is presented in green.
Moreover, the ABT RSQ8-LE 1000 also features enhanced aerodynamics. The novelties include the splitter, front skirt and hood inserts, wheelhouse ventilation at the front, door mirror casings, and B-pillar covers. The fender extensions, door strip attachments, rear skirt add-ons, rear skirt inserts, and wing with aero blades have also come from ABT Sportsline’s portfolio, and some of them have a matte carbon look.
The changes continue on the inside, where the steering wheel, which was wrapped in Alcantara, and the shift paddles, shift knob cover, dashboard covers, and seat frame covers in matte carbon, are mentioned. Other highlights include the dedicated door sills, a special logo on the center console, a new start-stop switch cap, ABT and RSQ8-LE logos on the seats, floor mats with embroidered RSQ8-LE logos, and trunk mat.
ABT’s RSQ8-LE 1000 represents the final chapter in the tuner’s trilogy, and it is capped at only 30 units worldwide. The tuner’s Instagram post embedded at the bottom of the page does not mention the pricing, but its official website does. And in order to turn your Audi RS Q8 into the ABT RSQ8-LE 1000, you will have to spend 165,000 euros overseas. This equals a little over $185,000 at the current exchange rate.
Photo: Instagram | abt_sportsline Mind you, that does not include the installation, which is another 20,000 euros (~$22,500), including tax, so you are looking at 185,000 euros ($207,850) in total. And no, that does not include the donor vehicle. As for the complete vehicle, you will have to spend a whopping 345,000 euros (equal to $387,610). And that’s Lamborghini Urus SE Performante territory, though between us, the ABT RSQ8-LE 1000 will smoke it all day, any day.
The Audi RS Q8’s Italian cousin has 812 ps (801 hp597 kW) combined from its plug-in hybrid 4-liter twin-turbocharged V8 and 1,000 Nm (738 lb-ft) of torque, taking 3.3 seconds to hit 100 kph (62 mph), and maxing out at 312 kph (194 mph). The Urus SE Performante has an electric driving range of 60 kilometers or 37 miles.
A brand new Audi RS Q8 Performance will set you back a minimum of $139,700 (equal to 124,325 euros) in the United States of America for the 2027 model year, and it kicks off at 146,200 euros ($164,255) for the regular RS Q8 and 160,000 euros ($179,760) for the RS Q8 Performance in its homeland of Germany.
Now, if you found yourself sitting on almost $400K and you wanted a cool super crossover for daily duties, would you really blow that much money on the ABT RSQ8-LE 1000? That’s a tricky one, as while it will smoke not only the Lamborghini Urus, which is based on the same platform, but also the Ferrari Purosangue and the Aston Martin DBX, but in the end, it is still an Audi, albeit one that carries an extremely exotic price tag.
